title: City of Sullivan holds public comment meeting for how federal funding should be spent - NewsBreak
text:
By Noah Gastineau ,
47 minutes ago
SULLIVAN, Ind. (WTWO/WAWV) — Residents in Sullivan County had the chance to help decide how to spend 6.3 million dollars in disaster recovery funding to continue recovery efforts from an EF-3 tornado that struck Sullivan County in 2023.
The funding is part of the Community Development Block Grant-Disaster Recovery funding from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. One of the residents who attending the open discussion meeting was Mattie Phegley. She survived the tornado back in 2023 along with her family and, at the time, her one-week-old daughter.
"We were in my small, small bathtub, sheltering her with our lives, and I just remember praying God, you can take me, but don't take my baby," Phegley said. "For her to be here today and healthy, that's what matters to me and that's why I'm here tonight."
The money comes from the federal government to help the city and county continue to recover. Sullivan mayor JD Wilson was excited about the turnout.
"They have the thoughts, they have, what they want to see these funds go towards," Wilson said. "I thought this workshop for them, open house here would be the first step in the right direction, we got a lot of great information here, a lot of them came with already arranged ideas that they were going to present to us tonight. I'll look forward to rolling this up and really breaking it down. It was just a data collection night."
This discussion helped shed light on what could still be improved.
"The housing infrastructure, community parks and rec," Wilson said. "There's several categories that starts at the top of the line and you start looking at and then you can filter it down from there, the specific projects."
Phegley also hopes some of the money can go towards helping the community. That includes things like sidewalks and trees to help revitalize the neighborhood she lives in as well as other neighborhoods.
"I also think we should have some trees out there to kind of make it less eerie," Phegley said. "Because to me, it kind of still looks like the storm just happened because we need to rebuild houses and trees and things like that down there. I do appreciate that they're trying to listen to us. I just hope that they actually do it tonight. So that does make me feel a bit better since after all this time, we're finally discussing the situation."
There is still time for people to submit their input on what the money should go towards as the City of Sullivan has an online survey people can take. If you are interested in taking the survey, click here .
